method: ocular media transmittance measured across 66 bird species; the text lists the swift among species with T0.5 of 380 nm or higher, without a value of its own in the part read

source.authors: Olsson P, Lind O, Mitkus M, Delhey K, Kelber A
source.title: Lens and cornea limit UV vision of birds - a phylogenetic perspective

where: Discussion, High variation in OMT (Table 1 holds the swift's own value as an image the fetch tool could not read)
quote: ...the common swift, the European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus), the mute swan (Cygnus olor)... have λT0.5 of 380 nm or higher...
note: A bound shared by a named group of species (swift, nightjar, mute swan, golden plover, great crested grebe, grey heron and several raptors), so graded g. The swift's own T0.5 sits in Table 1, which was not readable.
